transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… um, I’m here because I kind of scared myself, I guess. I’ve been having these thoughts—more than once—that maybe my family would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Not like… I don’t know, it’s hard to say out loud, but that’s what it is.

I kept trying to push it down and just go to work like normal, but it got heavy enough that I told my supervisor. I didn’t really know who else to tell, and saying it to him made it feel real. He thought I should come in and talk to someone, so… that’s why I’m here.
Have you ever felt this way before, or had similar thoughts or episodes in the past?

Yeah… I think so. Not always this bad, but if I look back honestly, these low stretches have been coming around for maybe about a year now. I didn’t really call them anything at the time—I’d just sort of tell myself I was tired, or work was getting to me, or I was just having a rough patch.

But this one… after my daughter left, it hit me the hardest. It felt different, heavier. Like the other times I could kind of push through and keep moving, but this time it’s been harder to shake off. So, yes, I’ve felt low before in the past year, but this is the one that scared me the most.
Before this most recent episode, were there any times in the past when you felt low or depressed for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I think there were. Looking back, I can see these low stretches have been coming and going for about a year now. At the time I didn’t really mark it on a calendar or anything, so I can’t tell you exact dates, but it wasn’t just a bad day here and there.

There were periods where it felt like I’d get stuck down there for a while, like I was just moving through everything heavy. I’d tell myself, “Just get through the week,” and then another week would pass and I’d still feel the same. So yes, before this most recent one, I do think there were times that lasted a couple weeks or more.

This one after my daughter left, though… that’s been the worst one. That’s the one that really knocked me down harder than the others.

Before the most recent episode, were there at least two separate times in the past when you experienced a low mood or other symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks and were significant enough to interfere with your daily life?

I think so, yes… I mean, I’m trying to be careful because I didn’t write it down or anything, but looking back, these low stretches have been coming around for about a year. It wasn’t just like I had one bad afternoon and then bounced back. It felt more like I’d get into this dip and stay there long enough that it started affecting how I was getting through my days.

Before this most recent one, I do think there were separate times where I was down for a couple weeks or more. I’d still show up and do what I had to do, mostly, but it felt like dragging myself through it instead of actually living normally.

This one after my daughter left has hit me the hardest, though. That’s the one that made everything feel heavier than before. But yeah, if you’re asking whether there were other stretches before this that lasted at least a couple weeks and got in the way… I’d say yes, looking back, there were.

Before this most recent low period, were there at least two separate times in the past when you felt down or had similar symptoms that lasted for a couple of weeks or more, and were clearly distinct from each other — meaning you had a period of feeling better in between them?

Yeah… I think there were separate times, if I’m looking back honestly. It’s a little hard for me to line them up neatly, because at the time I wasn’t thinking, “This is an episode,” or anything like that. I was just trying to get through work and get through the day.

But over about the past year, these low stretches have been coming around. And yes, there were times where I’d feel somewhat more like myself in between—maybe not perfect, but enough that it felt like I had come out of it some—then later I’d slide back down again. So they did feel separate, not just one straight year of feeling the exact same way every single day.

The most recent one, after my daughter left, has definitely been the hardest. That one hit me in a way the others didn’t. But before that, yeah… I’d say there were at least a couple of distinct low periods that lasted more than just a few days.
